row.notes: Pit stop update job, vtable slot 3 (ptr 0x1456236b8 in the table at 0x1456236a0; no direct calls). job+0x08 PitStopInstance, job+0x10 float dt. Returns early while PitStopInstance+0x64 is set. At 0x1403c0add it scales dt by PitStopInstance+0x3bc, the crew rate (while job+0x14 is 0 the sequence evaluate at 0x1403c07a1-0x1403c07d4 runs first, and its Start/Stop events can rewrite +0x3bc before that read), runs the PitStopLogic update (+0x330 vt+0x18) with the scaled dt, then Game_PitStopActionObserver_SetTransitionSequence (observer at +0x370). While +0x65 is clear (the transition call is skipped too while it is set) it then rewrites +0x3bc as factor x +0x33c (0x1403c1ab0, 0x1403c1f73), the factor set by the transition at +0x380 (1.0 by default; other transitions use other constants and clamped catch-up ratios); +0x33c is the base rate. Game_PitStopLogic_NeSequenceClipTargetImpl writes the crew speed from the pit lane car record *(pitlane+0x68+car*0x10) into both +0x33c (logic +0x14c, logic at +0x1f0) and +0x3bc on the sequence's Start event; Stop puts both back to 1.0, and so does SetTransitionSequence on every state change or forced call (on both sides of its +0x388 test), so a rate kept in +0x33c lasts only until the next state change, Start or Stop. So a rate written only to +0x3bc applies to the frame that reads it and is replaced at the end of the call; a rate that should persist goes in +0x33c. The scaled dt then advances the sequence instances: the crew sequence +0x3b0 while its flags +0x74 & 0x21 are clear, and +0x398/+0x3a0/+0x3a8 only while the bytes +0x390/+0x391/+0x392 are set (and their flags allow), each by instance+0x5c (the sequence time, float) += scaled dt x global scale (0x146046628) x resource+0x54 (the resource time scale). In game the time runs in seconds (the 1990 pit stop log: the crew speed, written by the Start event at 13/30 s of F1StartJobDoStandardStop258, is already set when the time reads 0.5), so +0x54 is about 1, not a frame rate. The instance's resource is instance+0x08, its name index resource+0x38 (g_Ne_NameTable); the update also reads a second name index at resource+0x3c (0x1403c0d4c).
